findings.summary: The work delivered is for the `canary-retry-proof` node (echo utility in scripts/echo.py and docs/echo-usage.md), not for the `job-state-consistency` node. The patch.diff modifies only scripts/echo.py and docs/echo-usage.md — neither file relates to jobs.status, queue_state, or database consistency. The decision.md documents an echo utility implementation, not the root cause of the inconsistent job row. No changes were made to engine.py (which has `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'expired'` without updating queue_state — the exact problem the node exists to fix). The required artifact `graph-update.yaml` is also missing. The `.gddp/` directory contains unrelated work for `neutral-executor-contract`. This is a complete node mismatch.

integrity.reasoning: The node `job-state-consistency` has the stated intent: \"Make jobs.status and jobs.queue_state agree on every write path.\" Its acceptance criteria require: (1) decision.md naming the write path that produced the inconsistent row job_20260711T16542651, (2) fixing every UPDATE to jobs.status in scripts/ (especially engine.py expiry) to also set queue_state, (3) creating a consistency check, (4) reconciling the stale row with documented SQL, (5) passing test suite. None of this work has been done. Instead, the root workspace contains a patch.diff that only modifies scripts/echo.py (adding embedded tests) and creates docs/echo-usage.md — this is the work for the `canary-retry-proof` node (echo utility). The decision.md describes an echo utility implementation. The `.gddp/` directory contains entirely separate work for the `neutral-executor-contract` node. The actual problematic code in scripts/runtime/decision_loop/engine.py (which does `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'expired'` without queue_state) remains untouched. No graph-update.yaml is present. This is a complete node mismatch — the wrong node's work was delivered under the wrong label. Both intent and graph integrity are fundamentally violated.
